cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a hand-woven aso oke strip-cloth man's gown (boubou/agbada) with chain-stitch embroidery at the neckline, a traditional West African style of dress widely worn by Wolof men in Senegal and neighboring groups; it plausibly fits the claimed ethnicity.

physical.title: gown; textile; tobe
physical.summary: Man’s gown (boubou, tobe, agbada). The body is formed of 24 aso oke strips hand-woven and hand-sewn together along the selvedges vertically, while the sleeves are sewn horizontally; the strips in the upper section are folded, and gradually unfolded below so as to make the skirt flare. The strips on the body and sleeves have the same design. This consists of alternating warp stripes of indigo within which are lines of single threads of white hand-spun cotton, and stripes of magenta (alaari) silk; the weft is indigo. The area around the opening of the neck is hand-embroidered in chain stitch on the front and back with lines of white cotton and four star-like squares or knots. The same decoration is embroidered around two vestigial openings on the chest. The neck opening is lined with plain blue cotton (possibly locally dyed), and the edge of the skirt is lined with pink and white machine-woven European printed cotton with a design of red and white stripes and red circles.
